So the vertical asymptote is between x = 2.6 and x = 3.4? Probably x = 3. The horizontal asymptote: as x → -∞, y → about 1? As x → +∞, y → about 1.5? Hmm.

At x = -8, y ≈ 0.8, approaching 1 from below as x → -∞? Actually, as x → -∞, k/(x-p) → 0 from the negative side if k > 0. Then y → q from below. Vertical asymptote at p: the left branch plunges to -∞ as x → p⁻, and the right branch goes to +∞ as x → p⁺. This happens when k > 0. Check: q = 1? Horizontal asymptote y = q. Left branch at x = -8: y ≈ 0.8; as x → -∞, y → q from below? If k > 0 and x - p < 0 then k/(x-p) < 0, so y < q. At x = -8, y = 0.8 < q. Right branch at x = 8: y = 1.45 > q. So q is between... hmm, as x → ∞, y → q from above: at x=8, y=1.45, so q is probably 1? Then k/(8-3) = 0.45 → k = 2.25. The curve crosses the x-axis around x = 1 (between 0 and 2). At x=0: f(0) = k/(-3) + 1 = 1 - 0.75 = 0.25. The graph at x=0 shows y ≈ 0.4-0.5? Hard to tell.

Maybe k = 2, p = 3, q = 1: f(0) = 2/(-3)+1 = 0.333; zero at x = 3-2 = 1. Matches crossing at x=1. At x=8: 2/5+1 = 1.4. Matches ~1.45. At x=-8: 2/(-11)+1 = 0.818. Matches ~0.8. So p = 3.

content:
Looking at the graph, the two branches of the hyperbola break apart near x = 3: the left branch plunges toward −∞ as x approaches 3 from the left, and the right branch shoots up toward +∞ as x approaches 3 from the right. This indicates the vertical asymptote is x = 3.

Checking with f(x) = 2/(x − 3) + 1: f(0) ≈ 0.33 (y-intercept just above 0), f(1) = 0 (x-intercept at 1), f(8) = 1.4 and f(−8) ≈ 0.82 (approaching horizontal asymptote y = 1), f(3.4) = 6 and f(2.6) = −4 (steep behavior near x = 3). All match the graph.

Thus the vertical asymptote parameter is p = 3.
